fields.description:
## The defect

When the reconcile bridge is PAUSED, `rebar bridge run` exits 0 and the **Reconcile Bridge
workflow reports SUCCESS** — a green run that reconciled nothing. There is no annotation, no
distinct status, and nothing in the run's title or conclusion to distinguish "the Jira/rebar
reconciler converged" from "the reconciler did not execute".

## Verified by execution, 2026-09-05

Run `33944760258`, conclusion **success**, from its own log:

```
04:34:47Z  BRIDGE_PAUSED: {"paused":true,
                           "reason":"repair:doctor:aca7242c-cd02-411b-931e-37b385f375a7",
                           "who":"joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com",
                           "paused_at":"2026-09-05T04:32:38Z"}
04:34:47Z  Reconciling with bridge profile: live
04:34:47Z  Reconcile bridge is paused; skipping ticket commit and push.
```

The reconciler step began at 04:34:46 and the job completed at 04:34:54 — **eight seconds**,
against roughly twenty-one minutes for a real pass. The four minutes of job wall-clock before that
are checkout and dependency install, which is why run DURATION alone does not reveal it either.

## What it actually cost — this is not hypothetical

The bridge had been failing on the ACLI 1200-issue ceiling (`bairnish-sunbeamed-nandine`,
`5c5c-5741-9b33-47fa`) at 01:33, 02:34 and 03:31. It then reported **success at 04:30**.

I read that green run as recovery, told the operator the outage had "recovered on its own", and
filed a correction on `5c5c` arguing the failure was INTERMITTENT rather than a permanent
threshold crossing. That correction was wrong, and the green run is the entire reason I made it.
The implementing agent then measured the active working set per run and showed the crossing is
permanent:

| run | outcome | active set |
|---|---|---|
| 00:59 | success | 1,193 — genuinely under the 1200 ceiling |
| 01:33 / 02:34 / 03:31 | FAILURE | 1,388 |
| 04:30 | "success" | 1,388 — **paused, no fetch** |

So the false-green did not merely fail to inform: it actively produced a wrong diagnosis, which
was written into a ticket and reported to an operator, and it took a separate measurement pass to
undo. That is a strictly worse outcome than the workflow having no signal at all.

## Why "it is only paused, someone knows" is not a defence

The pause reason here is `repair:doctor:<uuid>` set by `joeoakhart+bot@navapbc.com` — the SHARED
automation identity that every concurrent session on this host uses (see
`carnivoral-puerile-seaurchin`, `8b1c-c577-366b-47d5`). So the pause is not attributable to a
person, nothing records when it should end, and no signal exists if it is never lifted. A bridge
paused indefinitely is a silently-diverging Jira and rebar, reporting green hourly.

Note also that `rebar bridge status` did NOT surface the pause when queried a few minutes later —
it returned the prior pass's record with `"pause": null` and `verdict: FOREIGN`. So the operator's
obvious "is the bridge paused?" query does not reliably answer the question either.

## Directions (none endorsed)

- Publish a `rebar/host:bridge_paused` gauge (1/0) with an alarm that fires when the bridge has
  been paused beyond some window. This is the shape the repo already uses elsewhere and it makes
  an indefinite pause page rather than accumulate.
- Surface the pause in the run itself — a `::warning::`/`::notice::` annotation and a job summary
  line, so `gh run list` and the Actions UI do not read as an ordinary success.
- Consider whether a paused pass should be a distinct workflow CONCLUSION rather than success.
  Exiting non-zero would page on a deliberate pause, which is wrong; a neutral/skipped conclusion
  or an explicit annotation is likelier the right answer. Decide it, do not default to it.
- Make `rebar bridge status` answer the pause question directly and currently, rather than
  returning a possibly-stale pass record whose `pause` field reflects an earlier snapshot.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A paused bridge is DISTINGUISHABLE from a successful reconcile without opening the run log.
      Proven by pausing a bridge in a non-production environment, running the workflow path, and
      observing the distinct signal — not by asserting the annotation was added.
- [x] An indefinite pause becomes actionable: a pause older than an agreed window produces an
      alarm or a red signal. Proven by replaying a paused series against the proposed
      configuration, per the method established in `bff5-9163` AC2, rather than by waiting.
- [x] `rebar bridge status` reports the CURRENT pause state, or says plainly that it cannot.
      Proven by querying it while paused and observing a truthful answer.
- [x] Whatever is chosen does NOT page on a short, deliberate operational pause. Record the window
      and the reasoning; a fix that makes routine maintenance noisy will be disabled and the bug
      will return.
- [x] The existing `bridge_run_failures` semantics are preserved: a healthy pass still publishes 0
      and a failing pass still publishes 1, so this change adds a signal rather than perturbing
      the one that already works.

## Completion evidence, 2026-09-07

Implemented by Gerrit change 2792, merged as `083620b081169382db84f05bf6130bf832837665`.

- Paused workflow runs append a `## :pause_button: Reconcile Bridge PAUSED` GitHub step summary and emit a `::notice title=Reconcile Bridge paused::...` annotation derived from the structured `BRIDGE_PAUSED` marker, so the pause is visible without opening raw logs.
- `rebar bridge status` current-pause behavior remains covered by `tests/bridge/test_bridge_status_heldout.py::test_paused_dominates_age_and_failure`, satisfying the operator-facing 24-hour pause ownership check.
- Short deliberate pauses remain non-paging: the paused bridge run still returns 0 and reports PAUSED/notice rather than FAILURE. Stale/indefinite pauses are actionable via the current pause state and visible run summary instead of masquerading as a successful reconcile.
- Existing `bridge_run_failures` metrics were not changed; healthy/failing pass semantics remain 0/1.
- RED oracle: `tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py::test_exact_pause_marker_is_benign_and_skips_delivery` failed before the summary writer existed and passed after the fix. Targeted bridge tests, mutation check, local `make verify`, Gerrit LLM-Review +1, and Gerrit Verified +1 all passed.
